# ShelfSpace
> System for cannabis dispensaries — AP, consignment, and credit recovery on one Metrc-verified platform.
> Website: https://shelfspace.pro
> Login: https://ourshelf.space/login
> Contact: https://shelfspace.pro/contact
> Email: support@shelfspace.pro

## Account Access
Existing ShelfSpace customers log in at https://ourshelf.space/login (also reachable at https://shelfspace.pro/login, which redirects to the same place). New dispensaries start at https://shelfspace.pro/contact. The login URL for the ShelfSpace app/dashboard is https://ourshelf.space/login.

## What ShelfSpace is
ShelfSpace is a cannabis-specific system for profit optimization — accounts payable, consignment settlements, and vendor credit recovery on one platform, all reconciled to Metrc. Every SKU on a dispensary shelf is supposed to hit a margin; ShelfSpace makes sure it does — three-way matching every invoice against the delivery and the PO before the retailer cuts a check, building monthly credit memos for returns/expirations/co-marketing, running weekly consignment settlements, and answering vendor emails with live data through the ShelfiQ AI.

The fight every cannabis retailer is in: vendors overcharge, products expire, credits never get filed, invoices get duplicated, cash gets trapped on shelves, and the margin the retailer bought disappears. ShelfSpace catches the leaks at the SKU level so the dollars that should land in the retailer's account actually do.

## What is ShelfSpace? (operational summary)
ShelfSpace is a cannabis-specific system for profit optimization. The platform handles accounts payable as the spine — invoice ingestion (ShelfiQ parses vendor email), three-way matching (invoice ↔ delivery ↔ PO) against Metrc, per-vendor payment terms (COD, Net 30, Net 60, consignment, configurable per vendor), Check 21 payment generation (the retailer signs and sends the check), and vendor-email handling via ShelfiQ — ShelfiQ answers first-line questions in seconds; the 5% needing judgment surface in the platform with the full thread + data attached for the retailer's AP person. The platform expands into consignment settlements (weekly POS/Metrc reconciliation, vendor portal, retailer-driven vendor relationships) and credit recovery (monthly memos for returns/expirations/co-marketing — $20 per credit memo recovered, no percentage; retailer's AP person handles vendor pushback and negotiations). The platform works alongside the retailer's buyer (who keeps product selection, vendor negotiation, sell-through analysis, promotional planning) and the retailer's bookkeeper or accounting firm (who keeps month-end close, bank reconciliations, payroll, journal entries, financial statements, tax prep, 280E compliance).

Founded by Chris Mitchem, a 10-year cannabis operator who built ShelfSpace to solve the problems he lived with every day. Not a tech company — an operator who got tired of the broken system.

## Three Services

### Accounts Payable (https://shelfspace.pro/accounts-payable)
- Service walk: invoice ingestion (ShelfiQ parses vendor email) → Metrc verification of received quantities → over-pay protection (no check leaves until math holds) → ShelfiQ handles first-line vendor email (under-a-minute replies) → bookkeeper hours freed → vendor portal access. Every dollar paid maps to a SKU the dispensary actually got.
- Cannabis AP system — three-way matching on every invoice (invoice ↔ delivery ↔ PO), platform-generated Check 21 payments (retailer signs and sends), ShelfiQ vendor email handling, QuickBooks sync
- Per-vendor payment terms: pay Vendor A on COD because they require it, Vendor B on Net 30 because the relationship is established, Vendor C on consignment because you want sell-through visibility. All configurable from one workflow, switchable when relationships change.
- Cannabis and non-cannabis vendors — landlords, agencies, consultants, anyone
- Onboard vendors by email — the W-9 is collected right in the invite (no chasing, no faxing); no bank account numbers needed for the default Check 21 check (ACH direct deposit is opt-in, and the vendor links their own bank)
- Every vendor gets a free portal to download checks, view payment history, and track status; vendors who prefer paper can be opted in by the retailer to receive a physical check by mail instead of digital portal delivery
- Retailers cut every check on the platform — nothing goes out without their sign-off
- Vendors email the platform with questions; ShelfiQ answers first
- Saves approximately $45,000 per year in labor, errors, and missed credits at a single-store baseline

### Consignment (https://shelfspace.pro/consignment)
- One of the payment terms the platform runs — vendors carry inventory on a retailer's shelves with zero upfront cost; the retailer pays only when product sells at the register
- The platform runs the weekly settlement cycle: pulls POS data, reconciles against Metrc, calculates profit splits, generates six-page settlement reports (sales, margin analysis, waste, remaining inventory, plus the check itself), and queues Check 21 compliant checks for every vendor — the retailer approves and sends
- Role split: the platform runs the settlement engine (POS ingest, Metrc reconciliation, math, payments, vendor portal, reports, QuickBooks sync); the retailer owns vendor outreach, contracts, and disputes
- Vendor setup: each vendor record holds two settings panels — Wholesale Settings (AP payment terms) and Consignment Settings (Master Vendor Split, Operational Discount Budget, per-category splits, Settlement Frequency — Weekly / Biweekly / Monthly). Configure once; every consignment delivery and settlement from that vendor inherits the settings.
- Same vendor, two modes: the same brand can ship a retailer a consignment delivery and a wholesale delivery on the same day. Each delivery is one Order Type, one invoice, one Metrc manifest. Two manifests at the dock is a Metrc chain-of-custody discipline as well as a platform discipline.
- Order Type designation at delivery creation is the differentiator: tap Wholesale or Consignment on the Create Delivery form. Consignment-tagged deliveries get every SKU tracked individually for per-delivery payout; wholesale-tagged deliveries feed AP on the vendor's payment terms.
- Receive flow is identical whichever Order Type: upload signed paper invoice + Metrc manifest, confirm physical line-item dispositions (Received/Short/Damaged/Not Compliant), confirm the dollar total. Short/damaged/non-compliant adjustments flow into the settlement.
- Two-path payday: Approve & Pay tells the platform to cut a Check 21 from the retailer's bank, sync QuickBooks, and email the vendor a settlement report ending with the printable check. Mark as paid externally records that the retailer paid the vendor outside ShelfSpace (own check / ACH / cash); the platform records the resolution, no Check 21 cut, and the vendor's settlement report ends with a PAID EXTERNALLY stamp instead of a check page.
- Frees up approximately $250,000 in capital for the average dispensary (based on $2M annual revenue, 50% COGS, 90-day inventory on hand)
- The vendor owns inventory until it's sold — zero inventory risk for the retailer
- Unsold product can be returned to the vendor at no cost
- $20 per consignment payment — each settlement payout the platform runs and you approve. Free to start, no flat fee, no minimums. Pairs naturally with AP but is billed separately.
- Full step-by-step receiving and payout SOP: https://shelfspace.pro/docs/consignment/receiving-and-payout

### Credit Recovery (https://shelfspace.pro/credit-recovery)
- ShelfSpace identified $200,000+/year in vendor credits at a two-location chain
- Three types of credits recovered: product returns, expired product, and co-marketing/promotional credits
- We read your Metrc data and your monthly Dutchie reports, build credit memos line by line every month, and send them to vendors. ShelfiQ handles basic vendor questions; escalations route to the retailer's AP person or buyer for line-by-line negotiations and judgment calls
- $20 per credit memo recovered — flat, charged when the credit is applied, no subscription, no percentage of what's recovered. Free to start.
- At our Massachusetts client, identified unrecovered credits in the $8K–$25K/month range — the recovered credit dwarfs the $20 memo fee
- The platform does the data work and the initial outreach; ShelfiQ handles basic questions; the retailer's AP person or buyer handles vendor pushback and judgment calls
- Self-serve generation: retailers can build a whole month of credit memos themselves in the portal — a six-step wizard (pick a closed month, upload four Dutchie reports, read-only pre-flight, map vendors, generate, done) drafts one credit memo per vendor into Credits → Drafts to review and send; Dutchie-only report ingestion today, requires credit recovery enabled + an admin role
- Interactive calculator available at https://shelfspace.pro/credit-recovery to estimate recovery potential

## Payment System
- Three delivery methods, retailer picks per vendor: digital check (Check 21, portal download — the default), physical mailed paper check (opt-in), and ACH direct deposit (opt-in; the vendor links their own bank). All three deliver the same $20 payment artifact — ACH is not a separate charge and is free to vendors.
- All checks are Check 21 Act compliant — valid Substitute Checks under Federal Law
- Checks are print-at-home legal and mobile deposit ready
- ACH is opt-in and vendor-controlled: the retailer enables it, the vendor links a bank themselves, and ShelfSpace does not keep the vendor's full account number on file; the "no bank info required" trust story holds because Check 21 stays the default (see https://shelfspace.pro/ach)
- Every payment syncs to QuickBooks in real time — no manual journal entries
- Full audit trail on every transaction — who created it, when issued, when downloaded, current status
- Void a check and re-pay the order to issue a replacement with a fresh date and new check number

## Vendor Portal
- Every vendor gets a free portal at no cost
- Features: instant check downloads, complete payment history, real-time notifications, multi-retailer dashboard
- Vendors working with multiple ShelfSpace retailers see all their data in one view
- Cannabis and non-cannabis vendors supported

## Pricing (https://shelfspace.pro/pricing)
- Free evaluation: connect Metrc account, analyze historical data, receive a detailed report on what AP is leaking, what vendors owe, and what's trapped in inventory, plus a personalized onboarding plan. No commitment, no credit card.
- Pricing model: flat $20 per artifact. Free to start — the platform and signup cost nothing; you pay $20 only when the platform produces a billable artifact. No subscriptions, no software seat licenses, no percentage of recovered dollars, no flat monthly fee. Month-to-month, cancel any time. After the free evaluation and signup, the platform is self-serve — the retailer drives it; ShelfiQ handles first-line vendor email, escalations route to the retailer's AP person.
- Wholesale Payment ($20 each): per vendor payment generated on the platform (AP). Includes invoice processing, three-way matching, per-vendor payment terms, Check 21 payment generation (the retailer signs and sends), ShelfiQ vendor email handling, QuickBooks sync, vendor and operator dashboards, Metrc integration.
- Consignment Payment ($20 each): per consignment settlement payout the platform runs and the retailer approves. Includes weekly settlements, sell-through reporting, vendor portal. Retailer owns vendor contracts and outreach.
- Credit Memo ($20 each): per vendor credit memo recovered through credit recovery — built from Metrc-backed line items (returns, expirations, co-marketing) and charged when the credit is applied; no percentage of recovered dollars. ShelfiQ handles basic vendor questions; escalations route to the retailer's AP team. At our Massachusetts client, identified unrecovered credits in the $8K–$25K/month range.
- Volume discounts: multi-location and high-volume operators get volume discounts, set during onboarding.
- ShelfSpace works alongside the retailer's buyer (who keeps product selection, vendor negotiation, sell-through analysis, promotional planning) and the retailer's bookkeeper or accounting firm (who keeps month-end close, bank reconciliations, payroll, journal entries, financial statements, tax prep, 280E compliance). The platform handles the AP plumbing between them.
- For comparison context: a generalist bookkeeper at 1–5 location dispensaries costs $20–25/hour and typically spends 10–15 hours/week on AP. Outsourced cannabis accounting firms charge $75–150/hour, with AP as a high-cost line item. ShelfSpace's flat $20-per-artifact pricing runs well under the cost of the bookkeeper hours it frees.
- No contracts, no minimums, cancel any time. Vendors never pay.

## Technology
- Integrates with any cannabis POS system: Dutchie, Flowhub, BLAZE, Cova, Treez, Alleaves, MJ Freeway, Meadow, IndicaOnline, and more
- POS integration via CSV upload (any POS that exports sales data)
- Metrc compatible — inventory manifested in Metrc using existing protocols
- QuickBooks sync on all payments
- ShelfiQ AI advisor built in — ask questions about vendors, inventory, settlements, and credits in plain English
- Row-level security, multi-tenant data isolation, zero hard deletes
- Cloud-based, available anywhere cannabis is legal in the United States

## Case Study
A two-shop dispensary chain in Massachusetts:
- $200,000+/year in vendor credits identified
- 50+ MA vendors paid through ShelfSpace today
- $45,000/year saved on AP and operations payroll
- Vendors transitioned to consignment to free up capital
- Vendors report improved payment reliability and portal access

- Never Pay Full Price for Stale Cannabis Product (manifest-first receiving — cannabis is perishable but the invoice charges full price whether product was packaged last week or last quarter; the platform matches every Metrc manifest to a delivery BEFORE it can be received, then reads the packaged date on each package and flags anything older than the retailer's freshness rule for that category — defaults Flower/Pre-Rolls 60 days, Concentrates/Vapes/Edibles 120, tunable by category/vendor/SKU; keyed on PACKAGED DATE not expiration, which cannabis transfers rarely carry; the Confirm Physical Receipt dialog flags stale product, quantity mismatches (invoice qty vs manifest qty), and on-invoice-not-on-manifest lines in plain English; the retailer rejects the flagged package during Metrc acceptance and it goes back with the driver, comes off the invoice through the existing receive cascade, and the vendor gets an itemized notice; a pre-arrival email warns before the truck arrives; works on wholesale AND consignment (consignment is a swap/pickup not a credit); deterministic platform checks, not ShelfiQ): https://shelfspace.pro/blog/cannabis-inventory-freshness
- Cannabis ERP for Dispensaries: What You Actually Need (the honest answer to whether a dispensary needs a cannabis ERP — ERPs like Distru, Canix, and Flourish run the supply chain: cultivation, manufacturing, distribution, seed-to-sale tracking; a dispensary buys and sells product, so it doesn't run a supply chain; the money problems start after product lands — vendor payments, AP, credit recovery, consignment — which is what neither a POS nor a supply-chain ERP was built for; ShelfSpace is NOT an ERP, it's a cannabis-specific back-office system that runs alongside your POS (and your ERP, if you have one); three-actor map: ERP = supply chain, POS = front of house, ShelfSpace = back-office money): https://shelfspace.pro/blog/cannabis-erp-system

- Why getting advance approval from your vendors improves your margins (pre-approving a promotion with the vendor before it runs flips who funds the discount; on a wholesale/AP vendor the discount becomes a co-marketing credit on the monthly memo — and a pre-approved credit moves forward on vendor silence (auto-applied or staged for the retailer's one-click approval, per vendor) while un-pre-approved co-marketing always needs explicit yes; on a consignment vendor it adds a promotional allowance to the Operational Discount Budget so within-budget markdowns come out of the vendor's weekly settlement and the retailer stays above target margin; the platform matches every POS discount to the pre-approval record, builds and sends the credit memo, and ShelfiQ can create the promotion from an email; three pre-approval paths — portal, recorded evidence, AP bot): https://shelfspace.pro/blog/advance-vendor-approval-protects-margins
- Return and Waste Credits: the one vendor credit that applies to every order (defective vendor-side returns and Metrc-recorded destruction are a loss on a unit that was supposed to sell; the ONLY credit type that applies to BOTH consignment and wholesale product, because it is not a discount; math = unit cost × quantity × return policy rate, default 100%; only vendor-side return reasons count — defective, unsatisfied, faulty hardware — changed-mind returns stay with the retailer; every line tied to a Metrc package tag; on consignment the share is netted through the weekly settlement, not billed as a wholesale credit): https://shelfspace.pro/blog/returns-and-waste-vendor-credits
- Co-Marketing Credits: splitting the promotion with wholesale vendors (WHOLESALE ONLY — on consignment the vendor's split already shares every discount, so consignment gets returns/waste only; only PRE-APPROVED promotions are eligible and retailer-run markdowns (loyalty, employee, POS adjustments) are never charged to a vendor; math = (keystone − sale price) × co-marketing rate, where keystone = cost ÷ (1 − target margin) and defaults are 50% margin / 50% co-marketing rate; a pre-approved credit moves forward on vendor silence, an un-pre-approved one never does): https://shelfspace.pro/blog/co-marketing-vendor-credits
- Inventory Aging Credits: sharing the markdown on slow wholesale stock (WHOLESALE ONLY, like co-marketing — consignment gets returns/waste only; fires when a package ages past its threshold AND sells below keystone, no promotion required; default thresholds 60 days for Flower/Pre-Rolls/Concentrates and 120 days for Vapes/Edibles/everything else, precedence SKU > vendor > category > platform default; math = (keystone − sale price) × aging coverage rate; guardrail: an aged sale carrying a retailer POS discount — loyalty/employee — is EXCLUDED because vendors never fund the retailer's own programs): https://shelfspace.pro/blog/inventory-aging-vendor-credits
- Setting Your Target Margin and Coverage Rates (the four numbers that drive every vendor credit: target margin sets keystone = cost ÷ (1 − margin), default 50% = 2× cost, entered as a MARGIN not a markup; co-marketing rate default 50% wholesale-only; aging coverage rate inherits co-marketing if unset, can be higher, wholesale-only; return policy rate default 100% applies on both wholesale and consignment; aging thresholds 60/120 days by category, precedence SKU > vendor > category > default; the retailer sets terms unilaterally and they take effect immediately — ShelfSpace runs the operations, does not broker the deal): https://shelfspace.pro/blog/setting-credit-recovery-rates

- Aged Inventory on Consignment (there is NO aging deduction on a consignment settlement — the vendor is paid their split of what the item actually rang up for, so a markdown is shared automatically at the register; the old per-category aging discount tiers and the margin-deficit true-up were REMOVED in July 2026; markdown cost-sharing is wholesale-only via price drops / inventory aging credits): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/consignment/aging-discounts
- How to Receive a Cannabis Consignment Order (step-by-step SOP: vendor settings — Master Vendor Split + Operational Discount Budget + per-category splits; Order Type designation at delivery creation — same vendor can ship Wholesale and Consignment on the same day; upload signed invoice + Metrc manifest; confirm physical receipt with disposition picker; payday with Approve & Pay cutting a Check 21 or Mark as paid externally recording an off-platform payment; vendor receives a multi-page settlement report either way): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/consignment/receiving-and-payout
- Approve & Pay vs Mark as Paid Externally (decision-criteria deep-dive on the two ways to resolve a consignment settlement: Approve & Pay cuts a Check 21 + syncs QuickBooks + charges per-check fee + vendor receives printable check; Mark as paid externally records off-platform payment + no Check 21 cut + no QBO sync + no fee + vendor receives stamped report; reversibility + decision criteria + QuickBooks gotcha for bookkeepers explained): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/consignment/approve-pay-vs-paid-externally

### Credit Recovery
- How Credit Recovery Works (returns + expirations + co-marketing tracked into monthly vendor credit memos): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/overview
- Generate Credit Memos Yourself — Self-Serve (six-step in-portal wizard: Period → Upload reports → Pre-flight → Map vendors → Generate → Done; retailer picks a closed month, uploads four Dutchie exports — Returns Report, Discount Detail Report, Inventory Receipt Report Detail, Current Inventory — a read-only pre-flight validates the files and writes nothing, unmatched brands are mapped to vendors and remembered next month, then the platform builds one credit memo per vendor into Credits → Drafts for review and send; requires credit recovery enabled + admin role; Dutchie-only ingestion, closed months only): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/self-serve
- How to Configure Your Credit Recovery Settings (the Credits → Settings tab, set once before the first batch of memos; Credit Recovery Defaults card holds the coverage rates the platform uses to size each memo — Target Retail Margin 50% below-keystone line, Returns / Waste Coverage 100%, Co-Marketing Coverage 50%, Aging Markdown Coverage defaults to each vendor's co-marketing rate, flat $20 Credit Memo Fee; defaults apply to every vendor unless overridden, Default Terms card pushes a rate onto all existing vendors at once; Categories on the report toggles pick which credit types the wizard drafts — Returns & Destruction / Co-Marketing / Aging Markdowns & Price Drops; Auto-Approve on Silence switches per category default OFF, so on vendor silence a documented credit parks for the retailer's review; turn a category on to auto-book that credit type when a vendor doesn't reply within the review window; Email approved credit memos to my team sends each approved memo with a CSV summary + PDFs to accounting recipients as-each-approved or batched; then review Drafts and Send to Vendor): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/settings
- Send Approved Credit Memos to Your Accounting Team (get the paperwork to a bookkeeper who works outside ShelfSpace: the platform auto-emails each approved credit memo — a CSV summary spreadsheet + the memo PDFs — to your accounting recipients as-each-approved or on a weekly/monthly UTC digest; on demand, select memos on the Approved tab and Download ZIP or Email to Accounting; a single memo attaches the CSV + PDF directly, a digest bundles the PDFs in a ZIP; every PDF is rendered fresh to the approved amount so document and spreadsheet agree; Mark Applied records a credit settled outside ShelfSpace — moves it to the Applied tab with an "Applied (outside ShelfSpace)" badge, drops it from the payment picker, Undo reverses it; a flat $20 credit memo fee applies on auto-generated memos only, grandfathered/fee-waived accounts pay nothing; consignment-return credits are excluded — they net at the weekly settlement; retailer-admin only): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/accounting-export
- Read Your Credit Recovery Scorecard (the Credits → Scorecard tab: four KPI tiles — Credit Identified, Credit Requested, Credit Approved, Recovery Rate; recovery rate = approved ÷ decided credit, color-coded green/amber/red; a "Where to focus" callout naming the source leaking the most recoverable credit and the fix; Credit Funnel by Month + Requested Credit by Source charts split across returns & waste / co-marketing / inventory aging, per-source cards, and a monthly detail table; range picker last month/6/12/all/quarter; display-only over monthly credit memos, excludes manual + consignment-return credits): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/scorecard
- Credit Recovery Onboarding — Getting Started (step-by-step onboarding from signing on to first monthly credit memos; vendor list, buyer kickoff, monthly cycle): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/onboarding-sop
- Return Credits (tracking returned cannabis products in Metrc and generating credit memos against vendor payments): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/returns
- Expiration Credits (monitoring expiration dates, flagging aging inventory, generating credit memos): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/expirations
- Co-Marketing Credits (tracking vendor-funded promotions / MDF / below-keystone deals and generating credit memos): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/co-marketing
- Inventory Aging Credits (aged wholesale inventory that sells below keystone earns a vendor credit even without a promotion; category-aware thresholds 60/120 days with SKU > vendor > category > default precedence, keystone shortfall × aging coverage rate, retailer-POS-discount exclusion; wholesale only): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/aging
- Price Drops (ask a vendor to cover part of a markdown on aged WHOLESALE product BEFORE dropping the shelf price; Opportunities tab finds aged SKUs cross-vendor and one-click sends the ask; vendor approves/declines from an emailed link, one reminder at 5 business days, moves to awaiting-retailer-review at 10; an approved request lands in "Price Drops Approved by Vendor" on the monthly credit memo vs "Not Approved" — both are billed, approval is what stops the dispute; category-aware thresholds 60/120 days with SKU > vendor > category > default; the proposed shelf price and %-drop toggle are display only and never set the credit; wholesale only): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/price-drops
- Credit Memo Approval Process (Draft → Pending Vendor → Approved → Applied lifecycle, three vendor choices Approve / Approve a specific amount / Decline all handled by ShelfiQ, 10-calendar-day-from-delivery window after which documented credits move forward on silence — applied automatically for vendors set to auto-approve, or staged as Ready for Approval for the retailer's one-click sign-off otherwise; 60-day vendor dispute window): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/approval-workflow
- Does ShelfiQ Answer Vendor Questions on My Credit Memos? (yes, automatically, for every memo sent — no setup, does NOT depend on an AP inbox/auto-responder; credit-memo replies route to ShelfiQ, which recognizes the vendor + memo, answers from real returns/destruction/amount data, and drives to Approved / a partial amount / Declined; retailer stays off the thread but sees the full conversation in-portal and is notified on resolution; AP inbox is a separate wholesale-invoice feature; caveats: brand-new vendor email addresses may not auto-recognize, unsubscribed vendors may have some automated messages suppressed): https://shelfspace.pro/docs/credit-recovery/shelfiq-credit-memo-replies
